pairs.why: A keeps a smooth, soft background and a clean, outline-free body like the real cards, while B's cratered, pebble-strewn ground adds many background edges the real cards lack.
A has soft fuzzy bear edges and a plain smooth backdrop, while B adds stitched seams and background plank lines that add internal and background edges the real card does not have.
A's fins have few clean, crisp rim edges like the real fins, while B adds extra thin ridge lines on the blades.
The real calculator has dense, crisp small edges (digits and button rims), and B's lettered keys match that subject edge density, while A's blank chunky keys are too sparse.
B has finer, denser small-control edges (knobs, sliders, thin platter rings) like the real deck, while A's chunky, simplified shapes have far fewer internal edges.
A has the real card's bold, smooth glass rim and a few broad highlight edges, while B's fine bubbles and thin hairline edges are busier than the real card.
Both have similar crisp gold rims, thin metal stands and soft backgrounds, so edges give no reason to choose.
A's leaf clusters and curb are slightly bolder and simpler and its pavement is less busy, which is marginally closer to the real card's edge density, though the difference is small.
